# struktura

> struktura is a Rust crate for detecting structural anomalies in
> time-series data using Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (DFA). It computes
> the DFA scaling exponent (alpha) and its R-squared for any `f64` slice,
> compares it against a self-calibrated baseline, and reports a health
> verdict — with no hyperparameters to tune and no training data required.
> It is `no_std` + `alloc` compatible (default-features off; still requires
> a global allocator), has one required
> dependency (`libm`), and ships a CLI (`struktura`) plus a library API.

struktura detects when the STRUCTURE of a signal changes — not just when
values cross a threshold. It is used for spacecraft telemetry anomaly
detection, bearing/rotating-machinery fault detection, cardiac HRV
monitoring, GNSS scintillation detection, DevOps/production time series
health monitoring, financial regime detection, genome sequence structure,
and text-rhythm analysis. It has been tested against real NASA (SMAP/MSL,
IMS bearing run-to-failure, Voyager 1 magnetometer) and ESA (ESA-ADB Mission 1)
spacecraft telemetry datasets, and against the CWRU bearing dataset.

Algorithm: Peng et al., "Mosaic organization of DNA nucleotide sequences,"
Physical Review E 49(2), 1994 — a well-established statistical-physics
method for measuring long-range correlation structure, related to the
Hurst exponent.

## What it is NOT

- Not a frequency-domain tool (no FFT/wavelets) — DFA measures correlation
  structure, not frequency content.
- Not a point-anomaly/spike detector by itself — pair it with a residual
  detector for single-sample outliers.
- Not a trained model — there is nothing to fit; the baseline comes from
  the signal itself.
- Does not claim to run onboard any specific flight mission; it has been
  tested offline against public NASA/ESA telemetry datasets.
